organization design is an emergent process, that it is a process of self-organization, that it is an iterative process, and that it is a non-linear process.
the design of organizations should be based on the principles of emergence, self- organization and non-linearity.
the design of organizations is a process that emerges from the interaction of people, technology, and context.

how people act in organizations, how organizations emerge from the actions of individuals and groups, and how we can design for emergence.
how organizations are designed, how they are enacted, how they are changed, and how they emerge.
how organizations emerge from the actions of individuals and groups, and how they self-organize to create new forms and structures.

the OD community’s emerging assumptions about organization design are: (1) organization design knowledge is actionable; (2) organization design knowledge can be made actionable; and, (3) organization design knowledge should be made actionable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organization design knowledge is not actionable, but it is useful.
we are in the process of moving from the “old paradigm” of organization design to a “new paradigm” that is more consistent with the nature of the world in which organizations operate.
we are moving from the design and implementation of organizations as “things” toward the design of organizations as processes and systems of action.

the design of organizations is not a static, linear, and equilibrium process, but rather a dynamic, non-linear, and emergent process.
the community should embrace the new set of assumptions and develop new approaches to organization design that are consistent with them.
the community is moving from a focus on the “design of” to the “design for” and the “design with.”
